title: Lockjaw's tone and advice against overdoing solos
summary: McRae told Davis to cut down his overblowing and says Lucky Thompson lost his audience with long cadenzas.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: They were playing Selmers. See, but Eddie "Lockjaw" Davis at that time -- I kept telling him, I say --

Yeah, younger. I say, "You gotta get that tone straighten out." And he say -- when he was with Basie -- I heard him rehearse -- Basie going to the Apollo -- I walked to him, I say, "You finally got it like I told you." He say, "You like it?" I say, "Yeah! You straightened yourself out." When he went with Basie, boy, he would sound good, you know. I kept telling him, I say, "Don't overdo it. You're overdoing it. You're playing too much," you know.
